audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabrications and one enormous omission. (1) content.late says "Force Pulse's cooldown collapses in a fight because every nearby cast shaves 0.75s off it, so it's always up". No such mechanic exists. (2) breakdown.late says to 'Q-silence the counterplay' - Null Sphere has no silence. (3) Hallowed Mist is named the matchup-defining mechanic in six places ('never burn damage into it', 'Nothing here works through Hallowed Mist', 'schedule your pattern around its cooldown') and the page never once says what to actually do about it.
audit.why: Force Pulse draws energy from spells cast in Kassadin's vicinity and becomes usable only once it has charged; its cooldown is a flat 21/20/19/18/17s. Telling the reader it is 'always up' in a fight inverts the ability - they will plan a combo around an E that is not armed. On Hallowed Mist: Gwen can only be targeted by enemies who are INSIDE the mist, and Null Sphere is a targeted spell, so from outside it has no legal target. But Riftwalk is a ground-targeted blink, not a targeted spell - it lands inside the mist regardless, and once you are standing in it she is targetable again. That is the counterplay the whole page is built around needing and never states. The mist is also a stationary zone she can walk out of, and it is 22/21/20/19/18s.
audit.corrected: The 0.75s claim replaced with Force Pulse's real charge-from-nearby-casts mechanic and its 21s cooldown; the silence removed; and Riftwalk-into-the-mist written into mid, wants.you[1], the cooldown block and the interactions block, with the mist's 22s attached.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (E: 'draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity. Upon charging up...', cooldown 21/20/19/18/17; Q: 'fires an orb... at a target'; R: 'teleports to a nearby location')
champ-data/_kits/gwen.json (W Hallowed Mist: 'She can only be targeted by enemies who enter the mist', cooldown 22/21/20/19/18)

audit.whatIsWrong: win[5] (First item) reads Gwen, but whys[5] directly under it says 'My stall item plus a maxed Riftwalk flips it - I blink to dodge her commit and win the straight duel as she runs out of poke and her dash is down.' The chart and its own explanation say opposite things at the same stage.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 55% over 20 games, and the Rod-of-Ages window before Gwen's Riftmaker is the one bracket where his stats have arrived and hers have not. whys[5] describes that correctly; the chart entry was never updated to match. The 2+ items stage genuinely does belong to Gwen and all three sources agree there, so only the one stage moves.
audit.corrected: First item flipped to Kassadin in both layers to match whys[5]; spikes[2] rewritten from 'claw back to even' to the same reading so the two content fields stop disagreeing. 2+ items left with Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hallowed Mist, Skip 'n Slash and Needlework are all named as spikes and none of the three has a cooldown anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist is 22/21/20/19/18s - a genuinely long window once it is spent, which is what makes 'commit on its downtime' real advice rather than a slogan. Skip 'n Slash is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s, but the cooldown is partially refunded if she hits an enemy during the buff, so only a WHIFFED dash gives you the full window. Needlework is 120/100/80s. Snip Snip! is 6.5s down to 3.5s, which is why you never wait it out. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s.
audit.corrected: Mist's 22s, Skip 'n Slash's 13s plus the hit-refund condition, and Riftwalk's spread written into the spikes, mid and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemization line says 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' - wrong pronoun, and it never says what the sustain is or which item answers it.
audit.why: A Thousand Cuts heals Gwen for a portion of the bonus magic damage it deals to champions, so she is healing off every auto in a trade before Riftmaker is ever built. That is a Grievous Wounds problem, and naming the passive tells the reader why the item is mandatory rather than optional.
audit.corrected: Pronoun fixed and A Thousand Cuts named with Grievous Wounds against it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gwen.json (P: 'She heals for a portion of the damage dealt to champions by this effect')

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and winCon both call Gwen 'he' - 'He dives, you can't answer yet', 'out-blink every dive he commits'.
audit.why: These two strings are the first thing on the page. Boilerplate shared across the champion's other matchups leaked a male pronoun onto a female champion.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten in the right pronoun, and winCon re-pointed at the mist counterplay instead of repeating that nothing works through it.

edits.after: Riftwalk gives me a 5s blink to dodge her Skip 'n Slash all-in - and because it is ground-targeted, it lands inside Hallowed Mist, where she becomes targetable to me again.

edits.before: Level 6 is the swing. Riftwalk is a short, low-cooldown blink, so for the first time I can hop out of her E-dash all-in the instant she commits and dodge the jungler she's been setting up. Bait it: make her burn her E and step into Hallowed Mist chasing, then blink out so the Needlework slow whiffs and she's left out of position with no dash. Once my first stall item (Rod of Ages or a Catalyst) comes online and Nether Blade is refunding my mana, her Snip Snip! poke stops threatening to kill me and the lane settles to even. I'm not fighting for a lead yet — I'm closing the gap she built and getting to my items intact.
edits.after: Level 6 is the swing. Riftwalk is a 5s blink at rank 1, so for the first time I can hop out of her Skip 'n Slash all-in the instant she commits and dodge the jungler she's been setting up. It also solves the mist: Hallowed Mist only stops enemies OUTSIDE it from targeting her, and Riftwalk is ground-targeted, so I blink into the cloud and my Null Sphere has a target again. Her E refunds part of its 13s only if it connects, so a whiffed dash is the real window. Once Rod of Ages is online and Nether Blade is refunding mana, her Snip Snip! poke stops threatening to kill me.

edits.before: This is where I have to be honest: the full-build bracket leans back to Gwen. My kit looks scary on paper — Riftwalk goes near-spammable with Tear, Nether Blade refunds mana every on-hit, and Force Pulse's cooldown collapses in a fight because every nearby cast shaves 0.75s off it, so it's always up. Null Sphere's shield even blanks the non-true part of her burst. But her center Q is still true damage my shield and magic reduction can't touch, her Riftmaker gives her omnivamp sustain through my combo, and the moment I commit she drops Hallowed Mist and becomes untargetable — my blink-in burst whiffs and she resets the fight. I win this lane by being ahead BEFORE she's six-item: punish her mist on cooldown, don't facecheck into it, and don't gift her a kill that lets her out-scale me clean.
edits.after: This is where I have to be honest: the full-build bracket leans back to Gwen. My kit looks scary on paper - Riftwalk goes near-spammable with Tear at 2s a blink, and Nether Blade refunds mana every on-hit. But Force Pulse is not free: it only arms once enough spells have gone off near me, and it is still a 21-second cooldown once spent, so I get one cone per fight and I have to aim it. Her center Q is true damage my shield and magic reduction cannot touch, her Riftmaker gives her omnivamp sustain through my combo, and the moment I commit she drops Hallowed Mist - so blink INTO the cloud instead of bursting at it, because from outside she has no targetable hitbox at all. I win this lane by being ahead BEFORE she is six-item: punish the mist's 22 seconds of downtime, and don't gift her a kill that lets her out-scale me clean.

notes: Two fabricated mechanics removed. (1) content.late claimed "Force Pulse's cooldown collapses in a fight because every nearby cast shaves 0.75s off it, so it's always up". Riot's text: Force Pulse draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity and becomes usable only once charged, on a flat 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown. The page had the ability backwards and was telling the reader to plan combos around an E that may not be armed. (2) breakdown.late called Null Sphere a silence; Kassadin's Q has no silence. THE MISSING INTERACTION, and it is the whole matchup: Hallowed Mist stops only enemies OUTSIDE the mist from targeting Gwen. Null Sphere is a targeted spell so it has no legal target from outside - but Riftwalk teleports to a LOCATION, so it lands inside the mist regardless, and once you are standing in the cloud she is targetable again. Six separate strings told the reader that nothing works through the mist; none told them to step into it. Also added: Skip 'n Slash refunds part of its 13s only when it connects, so the whiff is the window. Anti-heal line fixed - A Thousand Cuts heals her off every auto, and the itemization string had called Gwen 'his'. tldr and winCon also mis-gendered her. LEVEL CHART: win[5] said Gwen while whys[5] said Kassadin 'wins the straight duel' at the same stage; flipped First item to Kassadin on a 55% win rate and rewrote spikes[2] to stop it contradicting whys[5]. Confidence Medium on that one stage - 20 games is a thin sample and spikes[2] had originally called it even.
